title: make expanded TITLE and BODY as make text, so $(shell ...) in them ran
resolution: The target unexports BRANCH, TITLE, BODY, and RESUME and passes their raw $(value ...) under other names, without MAKEFLAGS; a real make run with a stubbed script proves the arguments arrive as typed.

title: A reused ticket number let two runs that read the queue at once both hold the Docker slot
resolution: Tickets follow Lamport's bakery algorithm with a choosing marker and a never-reused path of number and unique run ID; step tests replay the reported interleaving.

title: Stale recovery freed the slot while the killed holder's command still ran
resolution: The holder leads a new process group that runs the command; a ticket is stale only when its process and its group are gone, tested with a command that outlives a killed holder.

title: The stamp key omitted the merge base that contract compatibility and findings validation read
resolution: The key covers the merge base with origin/dev, or none; a test with the same tree on a new merge base shows the stamp is not reused.

title: make integrate pushed after a make verify that wrote no stamp of the merged tree
resolution: The script requires a clean integration worktree (NOT CLEAN, exit 7) and, after a passing make verify, a full stamp of the merged tree before any push (VERIFY FAIL, exit 4).

title: The alarm killed only make and left the verify run and its children running
resolution: make verify runs as its own process group under a Perl supervisor that stops the whole group, TERM then KILL, and waits until it is gone; a test checks that no process survives.

title: A failed delete push or ls-remote was not told apart from a deleted branch
resolution: A failed delete push no longer aborts; a remaining branch exits 6 with DELETE FAILED, and a failed ls-remote exits 9 with DELETE UNCONFIRMED instead of LANDED.

title: A resume after a created pull request opened another one instead of continuing
resolution: The script looks up the branch's pull request with gh pr list, merges an open one, and only cleans up after one merged at the pushed commit; both resumes are tested.

title: The main clone was not checked before the remote merge and its pull
resolution: Before any remote change the script requires the main clone on a clean dev that origin/dev fast-forwards, else MAIN NOT READY and exit 8; three cases are tested.

title: make record-check accepted any hand edit of the recorded test counts and coverage
resolution: make record stores its generated verify line next to the run's stamp, and record-check requires the recorded line to equal it; a test edits every count and coverage figure.

title: The log parser mixed runs and accepted a passing stamp followed by a failure
resolution: The parser reads only the last run, from its profile line to the stamp line that must end the log, and refuses repeated, failing, or contradictory totals.

title: The delta left Integration tests in verification requiring npm test in every make verify
resolution: A MODIFIED delta limits that requirement and its scenarios to make verify of the full profile.

title: A detached HEAD could get the docs-only profile outside CI
resolution: A detached HEAD gets the full profile; the spec delta, design, and protocol name it, and a test covers it without CI.

title: The record listed the passed make verify and record as remaining and missed 16987d29
resolution: The revision, task ticks, and remaining gates now reflect make verify on f726edbf and record and record-check on 16987d29, and the citations follow the fixed code.

title: The design said CI is never stamped, although a CI run writes a stamp
resolution: The design now says CI never reuses a stamp: a CI run may write one, which nothing reads.

title: A poll read the tickets before the choosing markers, so two runs could still both hold the Docker slot
resolution: liveQueue reads the choosing markers before the tickets, as the bakery algorithm requires; a step test publishes the other ticket through an injected Processes.started hook during the poll and fails on the old order.

title: INT, TERM, or HUP killed the make integrate supervisor but left make verify running in its own group
resolution: The Perl supervisor stops the group on INT, TERM, and HUP (TERM, KILL after 10 s) and exits 128+n; the script forwards those signals, prints INTERRUPTED, and runs make verify from /dev/null; a SIGTERM test checks that no process is left.

title: A resume after GitHub merged the pull request with a merge commit merged origin/dev again and opened a second pull request
resolution: A run or resume whose HEAD is already in origin/dev only cleans up; the gh stub now merges with a real merge commit, and resume and fresh-run tests fail on the old script.

title: The integration-flow delta still required make test in every make verify
resolution: The requirement body now says make test runs in the full profile only, matching Docs-only verify profile; the body stays under 500 characters.

title: make -t verify or make -q verify wrote a stamp without running any check
resolution: isDryRun treats t, q, --touch, and --question like n; the test covers them.

title: The stale-holder check compared ps start times that depend on the caller's time zone and locale
resolution: ps runs with TZ=UTC and LC_ALL=C; a test reads this process's start time from a child in another time zone and locale and fails on the old code.

title: The context hook counted output tokens, which the design excludes
resolution: The estimate counts input, cache creation, and cache read tokens only, as design.md states, and the design names the exclusion; the tests now carry output tokens that must not count.

title: The record still said the pass 1 fixes had not run make verify
resolution: The stale sentence is removed.

title: Self-check citations of the Makefile and verification-record.ts no longer matched their targets after the merge
resolution: Every file:line citation of the self-check was rechecked against the fixed tree and updated.

title: RESUME=0 or any other non-empty value also resumed make integrate
resolution: The target passes --resume only for RESUME=1, the comment and protocol say so, and a real make run proves RESUME=0, yes, and empty start fresh.
